facts.fact: 次日早晨，他吩咐叙述者带他去阳台（Balcony）。
facts.anchor: The next morning, he bade me lead him to the Balcony.

facts.fact: 叙述者在阳台上再看时，进迷宫的那队人只剩三个：皇家审判官和两名仆人。
facts.anchor: There were only three of them now—the royal inquisitor and two servants.

facts.fact: 他递给叙述者一块方布，叙述者展开即知那是公主的围巾——公主的每条围巾都用纯金线在褶边绣着国王的徽记。
facts.anchor: I unfolded it, though I knew already what it was. All of the princess’s scarves bore the symbol of the king, stitched along the hem with threads of pure gold.

facts.fact: 审判官命令叙述者第二天护送他们去神庙。
facts.anchor: “Tomorrow you will escort us to the temple,” he said.

facts.fact: 次日早晨，他们发现审判官剩下的那名仆人也带着自己的飞马逃走了。
facts.anchor: In the morning, we discovered that the inquisitor’s remaining servant was possessed of more wisdom than the others; he and his pegasus were gone.

facts.fact: 审判官手持弓箭戒备，仿佛那能抵挡已经杀死他两名手下的东西。
facts.anchor: He had his bow out, as if that would defend him against whatever had killed two of his men.

facts.fact: 叙述者多年前亲手杀死了这位老女祭司；最初几年她的鬼魂一直跟着叙述者，近年才越来越少露面。
facts.anchor: In the first few years after I killed her, she had followed me incessantly, even sleeping next to me in the tent, or pantomiming sleep.

facts.fact: 叙述者整了整围巾抵挡女祭司身上的寒气，并同她打赌：审判官还能撑一个月，除非女神先厌倦他、把他弄死。
facts.anchor: I adjusted my scarf in a fruitless attempt to ward off her cold. “I say it takes him another month. If the Goddess doesn’t tire of him before then, and kill him.”
